sentences.text: Diomedeoides was an extinct genus of seabirds belonging to the order Procellariiformes, a group that includes modern albatrosses and petrels. It is currently the only genus known in the family Diomedeoididae.

Fischer described the genus Diomedeoides in 1985, establishing Diomedeoides minimus as its type species. Three species of this bird have been described in total. Two species are known from Central Europe, while a third species is known only from Iran.

Fossils of Diomedeoides date from the Early Oligocene to the Early Miocene. These remains have been found in Oligocene and Miocene rocks in Europe and Iran. The bird lived between 33.9 and 23.04 million years ago.
Researchers suggest that Diomedeoides may be a junior synonym of the genus Rupelornis. The parent group of Diomedeoides is the family Procellariidae.
